title: adding upgrade feature
body:
NOTE: setting this to merge into the `metrics_get` branch temporarily, in order to give a more accurate diff while https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/9 is still alive. Should be changed to master once https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/9 is merged.

This adds the final core feature to the project, a functioning upgrade button. Now if a user clicks the upgrade button, their account will be upgraded to the enterprise plan, all of their previously inactive users will be set to active, and the "successful upgrade" banner will flash onto the screen for 3 seconds as the upgrade button disappears.

On the frontend, this PR completes the full feature set. There are aspects of the UX that are clunky at this point -- the dashboard load can be awkward, with the number of users and existence of the upgrade button taking a small but visible time to initialize. It's possible for the "you've exceeded your limit" and "successful upgrade" banners to stack momentarily, and whether or not a banner is shown determines how high up the screen the progress bar is (it would be smoother if that height was fixed and the banners just showed up in empty space). But for the sake of getting to the unit tests for this project, I'm going to let those go for now.

The backend update is mostly straightforward: I've added an `UpdateSession` method to the `SessionManager` and an `UpgradeHandler` to handle calls to the "/api/upgrade" endpoint.

`database.UpgradeAccount` is novel in this codebase in that I use a transaction to ensure that the account upgrade from FREE to ENTERPRISE _and_ the updating of all that accounts' corresponding inactive users to being active both happen in the upgrade call, in order to ensure the data model doesn't get partially corrupted (i.e. the account is upgraded successfully to ENTERPRISE but the call to upgrade all of its corresponding users to active fails).

One tricky wildcard I believe I've found (based on running the app and examining the database afterwards) is that if a `CreateUser` is called during an `UpgradeAccount` transaction, that user can wind up being created with `is_active` set to `false` (if the account was above its user limit before being upgraded), and not get updated to `true` when the `UpgradeAccount` transaction completes. What I think is happening (but haven't confirmed) is that internally the database is setting up the transactions in-memory based on what was in the database when they were initiated, and then committing them based on that in-memory representation. So if a `CreateUser` runs right after line 34 in `UpgradeAccount`
```go
_, err = tx.Exec("UPDATE user SET is_active=$1 WHERE is_active=$2 AND account_id=$3", true, false, accountID)
// CreateUser executes here, before tx.Commit().
```
that newly minted user isn't included in the UPDATE. To solve this, I've added the `createUserUpgradeAccountLock`. That feels like a bit of a hack, but probably the best I'm going to get to for this project.

#### To test
Test this similarly to https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/9, but this time try clicking the "Upgrade" button.

title: Metrics get
body:
NOTE: setting this to merge into the `metrics` branch temporarily, in order to give an accurate diff while https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/8 is still alive. Should be changed to `master` once https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/8 is merged.

Adds the "api/metrics" GET endpoint on the backend and updates the Dashboard component on the frontend to poll for metrics and update the interface based on what is received.

#### To test
```
docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml up
```

Copy the token from the line that looks like
```
backend-dev     | 2021/01/16 21:54:50 Created fakeiot test account with account_id=testacct-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, username/pwd=test@goteleport.com, and token=_pRmtus88dEg2CGZA5GqQfzydUDu9yxYUkYUCjRC39o=
```

navigate to https://0.0.0.0:8080 and login with username/pwd=`test@goteleport.com`

In another terminal, run
```
export TOKEN=<token_you_just_copied>
fakeiot --token=$TOKEN --url="https://localhost:8000/api" --ca-cert=./certs/localhost.crt run --period=20s --freq=0.1s --users=100 --account-id=testacct-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```

Navigate back to your browser window and see the interface update in [close to] realtime. Run the `fakeiot` command above until 100+ users have been faked, and see the "maximum users" warning appear.

You can also check that the polling function handles session timeout appropriately by changing `"12h"` in `main.go` to something short like `"3s"`, i.e. 
```go
sessionTimeout := flag.String("sesh", "3s", "A parseable duration string (https://golang.org/pkg/time/#ParseDuration) specifying the absolute timeout value for user sessions")
```

Then log in again and see that after a few seconds, the client receives a 401 and subsequently redirects the user back to the login screen.

title: Metrics POST endpoint
body:
The PR adds the "api/metrics" POST endpoint (to be hit by fakeiot). To do so, I needed to add the `model/apikey.go` `model/metric.go` and `model/user.go` models to the schema, and their corresponding files in `database/` for manipulating them. 

`handlers/metric.go` makes use of these new functions to add users to the database as they come in from the `fakeiot` devices. The `metricsPostHandler` is also wrapped in the `WithAPIkeyAuth` middlewear to ensure the caller is sending a valid api key in Bearer token format via the Authorization header. 

I've also added `WithAPIHeaders` and WithHTMLHeaders` middlewear, and added a new util (which is now in its own package) named `ErrorJSON` which functions like `http.Error` but doesn't rewrite the "Content-Type" header to "text/plain" (which was the source of some major pain in trying to figure out what `fakeiot` was complaining about).

#### To test:
Run
```
docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml up
```
Once the backend is built, the Docker logs should print something along the lines of
```
backend-dev     | 2021/01/16 03:38:34 Created fakeiot test account with account_id=testacct-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, username/pwd=test@goteleport.com, and token=tXOSpmXIyAdycSWAJqRS-YMg4gEMQHSEfXY7MadP68Q=
```

Copy the token (aka API key) from that line (make sure it's the line corresponding to `account_id=testacct-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` and not the other one)

Then, assuming you already have [`fakeiot`](https://github.com/gravitational/fakeiot) installed locally, navigate to the repo in another terminal and run
```
fakeiot --token=$TOKEN_YOU_JUST_COPIED --url="https://localhost:8000/api" --ca-cert=./certs/localhost.crt test
```
and all tests should pass.

You can also run
```
fakeiot --token=$TOKEN_YOU_JUST_COPIED --url="https://localhost:8000/api" --ca-cert=./certs/localhost.crt run --period=5s --freq=0.1s --users=100 --account-id=testacct-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
a few times and then manually examine the sqlite database file and see that users are being added to the `user` table (with `is_active` set to false, once you get over 100 users) and metrics are being added to `metric` table.

title: Logout
body:
Changes `WithSessionAuth` to a middlewear that checks for the appropriate authorization header and checks that a valid `Session` exists (returning 401's if either doesn't check out), and then passes the `Session` as a value into the request's `context.Context`, allowing wrapped handlers to interact with Sessions via methods that pass in their` r.Context()` (currently onely `sm.DeleteSession` does this, but this should work generally).

Also addresses @awly's comments from prematurely-merged https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/5

title: Updates design document with more sensible system for the metrics endpoint
body:
I was initially confused about how the "/metrics" endpoint should work, but landed on something more coherent. 

This new design assumes that there is some external or yet-to-be-built system for account registration, and that we should only be receiving calls to "/metrics" from fakeiot devices that have a pre-registered `account_id`. I've added an `apikey` table to constrain api keys to individual accounts. 

(This PR also updates some mistakes in the account/user/logins tables)

title: Logout
body:
Adds logout functionality

## backend
Adds a goroutine-safe method `SessionManager.DeleteSession()` for deleting a session from the session manager, and the logout handler that calls it. For edge cases where the "api/logout" request is sent with a missing/improperly-formatted Authorization header, or the token sent in the Authorization header is not found in the `SessionManager`, I've elected to simply log the discrepancy and return a 204 success response to the client so that it still reacts the same as a normal logout (where a session of sessionID is deleted). Open to better ideas/security concerns.

## frontend
The frontend route structure is revamped to direct the user directly to the "/dashboard" route, which is now protected by an `<Authenticated>` wrapper. 

Note: In `<Authenticated>` (and elsewhere), I've elected to use conditional rendering with `<Redirect>` over the `useEffect` hook with `history.push`; unlike the `useEffect` approach, conditional rendering prevents the app from flashing the primary component on the screen before redirecting the user (e.g. see changes starting on lines 25/26 of `Login.jsx`)

## To test
To check manually that the `SessionManager` is behaving as expected, it can be helpful to add `log.Printf("%v", lh.sm)` to line 73 of `login.go` and line 34 of `logout.go`

Run
```bash
docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml up
```
and navigate to https://0.0.0.0:8080

Try navigating directly to each of
* https://0.0.0.0:8080
* https://0.0.0.0:8080/login
* https://0.0.0.0:8080/dashboard

while logged out, and see that they behave as expected. Login with username/pwd = `dev@goteleport.com` and check that you're redirected to the dashboard. 

Try each of the links above again and see that they behave as expected while logged in. 

Hit the "Logout" button and see that you're redirected to /login. Confirm that the `SessionManager` is behaving as it should via the log outputs.

title: Session management frontend
body: Follow up to https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/3 with a simplified global session context structure based on @alex-kovoy's review

title: Session management part 1
body:
# Session management part 1
This PR adds code for the database layer and the beginnings of the session management system on the `backend/`, and gives the `frontend/` a global state management system.

## `backend/`
I chose [`sqlx`](https://github.com/jmoiron/sqlx) as a `database/sql` wrapper because it appears to provide better developer ergonomics for marshaling data to and from the database and `structs`.

#### `package model`
`model` is the simplest new package, currently containing just a variable with the SQL statement for creating the account table and the corresponding `Account` struct. Initially `Account` was in the `database` package, but I later realized that I needed it in more than one place (namely, for the session manager in the `auth` package) and so moved it to it's own `model` package in order to solve cyclic import errors.

#### `package database`
`database` is naturally the package for initializing and interacting with the database. Right now it comes hardcoded to use `sqlite3` and I didn't focus at all on making it theoretically compatible with other RDBMS engines. `database.go` contains config and initialization, and `account.go` contains functions for interacting with the account table.

#### `package auth`
`auth` right now is something of an eclectic collection of functions and objects related to authentication. `genkey.go` has utility functions for generating cryptographically random session ID's (and in the future, API keys). `password.go` has the password hashing and hash-checking functions.

The meat of the package is in `sessionmanager.go`, which contains the beginning of an in-memory session manager. The idea is that there will be a single global `*SessionManager`, which will house all of the `Session`s in the `SessionManager.store` map (indexed by `SessionID`). 

In the future (next PR), auth protected endpoints will be sent the `SessionID` in the header, and the `SessionManager` will check that a valid session exists (using appropriate synchronization mechanisms) and then return a copy of the `Session` object. The handlers can then modify/use the `Session` objects as necessary, and then later if the `Session` object needs to be updated, the `SessionManager` can replace the corresponding value in the `store` (again using appropriate synchronization mechanisms).

## `frontend/`
The meat of the changes on the frontend are in `store.jsx`, where I set up a `React.Context.Provider` that is wrapped around the entire `<App />` to make a global `store` state available to any component that consumes it. I then modified `Login.jsx` to update the global store on login and switch to the `/dashboard` route when the user is authenticated.

This design is based on the description in this blog post [here](https://codeburst.io/global-state-with-react-hooks-and-context-api-87019cc4f2cf), with some added code to make use of `localStorage`.

(@alex-kovoy I haven't forgotten about [this](https://github.com/ibeckermayer/teleport-interview/pull/2#discussion_r552391932), planning to upgrade to that in the next PR)

# To Test
In order to realize the changes to the `backend/dev.Dockerfile`, you may need to rebuild the images by running `docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml build --no-cache` (just FYI, since this was causing me major headaches for a while). Then run
```bash
docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml up
```
and navigate to https://0.0.0.0:8080

If you try and login with any credentials other than username/pwd == `dev@goteleport.com`, you should receive an error. If you log in with the correct credentials, you should be routed to `/dashboard`. If you navigate to the app again in another tab, you should get routed quickly to `/dashboard` since the global store should be found in local storage.

You can visually confirm that the `SessionManager` is doing something that seems about right by adding
```go
log.Printf("%+v", lh.sm)
```
to line 72 of `backend/internal/handlers/login.go`

title: Docker-ized app setup
body:
Relatively large PR to nail down some of the core app structure, manage self-signed SSL, and run a Docker-ized development and production basic app.

To test:
- See the updated `README.md` for instructions for setting up the dev/prod environments. If anything is confusing or not adequately explained, the `README.md` should be updated.
- When you navigate to the app in the browser, you should see the login form:
  - Invalid email string (i.e. no "@" character), or empty email or password should cause the html5 form validator to complain (screenshot 1)
  - Invalid credentials should cause a 401 error message to display in the console (screenshot 2)
  - Valid credentials (username and password both `admin@goteleport.com`) should take you to the dashboard route (screenshot 3)
  - (Behavior should be exactly the same for both dev and prod setups)
